questions.prompt: What is the capital city of The Bahamas?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the The Bahamas article.

questions.proof: The country's capital, Nassau, is on New Providence Island.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with The Bahamas?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture The Bahamas on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography and climate” part of the The Bahamas article.

questions.proof: The closest island to the United States is Bimini.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of The Bahamas?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the The Bahamas article.

questions.proof: The islands' mostly Black population speaks English, the country's main language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “They moved into the southern Bahamas from Hispaniola and _____ around the 11th century AD, having come there from South America.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “around”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the The Bahamas article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: They moved into the southern Bahamas from Hispaniola and Cuba around the 11th century AD, having come there from South America.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Augustine in East Florida in September _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the eighteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the The Bahamas article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Augustine in East Florida in September 1783.
